notes: Severity is shown as a coloured square and a word, without a frame, in tables, lists, notifications and reports. Reds, greens and ambers come from one consistent set.

Conditional Access drift marks each change by direction: green for added or turned on, red for removed or turned off, and amber for a value replaced by another. An open finding stands apart from the findings around it.
The update notice and the What's new overlay are redesigned. Display preferences, toggles and switches share one design, and text is no longer separated with centred dots.

Finding, Alert and Case wording changes with the matching Backend release. The two updates can be installed in either order.
Guidance on how to fix a finding writes a path through a Microsoft portal with ">" between its steps, for example "App registrations > Authentication".
Headlines for privileged role grants read, for example, "Tier 0 role: Global Administrator". Extra roles in the privileged access list are written "(Permanent, Direct)".
No check was added or removed, and no severity changed. This update and the Portal update can be installed in either order.

Citations now read, for example, "supports Art. 21(2)(i): access control". The Azure check for Defender for Cloud plans is renamed to "No paid Defender for Cloud plan is enabled on any subscription".
Existing Alerts and Cases keep their original text. Findings show the new wording after the next scan.
Fallback wording is shorter and more specific when the local model cannot produce an acceptable answer, so a failed model attempt still leaves useful prose.
Finding and tenant explanations run through the bundled offline model. Opportunity explanations use reviewed copy directly, which avoids an unnecessary model run and its Azure compute cost.

Updating this bundle rewrites prose, never evidence. The release was run with networking disabled and passed the full draft evaluation. Numbers are composed by the product and stay outside the model's control.
